 This Mfa Is Filed U/S.173(1) Of Motor Vehicles
Act, Against The Judgment And Award Dated 23.08.2019
Passed In Mvc No.327/2017 On The File Of The Senior
Civil Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kushtagi, Allowing The Claim Petition For
Compensation And Seeking Enhancement Of
Compensation In The Interest Of Justice And Equity.
 This Appeal Is Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
With consent of learned counsel for parties, appeal is taken up for final disposal.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 23.08.2019 passed by learned Senior Civill Judge and M.A.C.T, Kushtagi in MVC No.327/2017, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

3. Shri S.C.Hiremath, learned counsel for appellants-claimants at outset submitted that occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle leading to death of minor Basavaraj S/o Mahadev aged 09 years is not in dispute.
Tribunal assessed compensation and granted inadequate compensation.
Same is not challenged by insurer.
It was submitted that in accident in question, minor Basavaraj aged 09 years was died.
Claim petition was filed by parents.
By referring to decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kishan Gopal Vs Lala and Others reported in 2014(1) SCC 244, tribunal awarded lump-sum compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

sentences.text: It was submitted that as minor boy died during treatment, medical expenses has to be awarded separately apart from compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.
4. While passing impugned award, tribunal has noted total of medical bill were for Rs.2,30,359/-.
Therefore, sought for award of same.

5. On other hand Shri N.C.Kolloori, learned counsel while not disputing legal position availing from decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Meena Devi (supra), would submit that on verification of medical bills, it was seen that there was addition of an estimate bill which could not be considered.

6. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award and records.
7.

From above submission, only point that would arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for ?"
8.

Though claimants in instant case are parents, Hon'ble Supreme Court while assessing compensation in Meena Devi's case (supra) has stated that annual income of minor non earning person has to be taken at Rs.30,000/- and multiplier of '15' to be applied.

To said sum Rs.50,000/-
was ordered to be added towards conventional heads.
Thus, it arrived at compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.
9. As per Ex.P9, claimant has produced medical bills.

Learned counsel for respondent- insurer upon verification of bills from certified copy made available by learned counsel for claimants- appellants submitted that total value of bills produced was for Rs.1,30,324/-, claimant would be entitled to said sum.
Thus, claimants would be entitled for total reassessed compensation of Rs.6,30,324/-.
Therefore, point for consideration is answered in affirmative.

10. In result, I pass following:
ORDER a.
Appeal is allowed.
b. Judgment and award dated 23.08.2019, passed by learned Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T, Kushtagi, in MVC No.327/2017 is modified.
c. Claimants are entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.6,30,324/- as against Rs.5,00,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
d. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
